newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine must determine currency regime - c.bank.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine must determine currency regime - c.bank.

text.p: Ukraine's central bank must decide on a new currency regime soon as the Ukraine Interbank Currency Exchange (UICE) is losing its importance on the currency market, a senior bank official said on Tuesday.

"The volume of trading on the UICE occupies 10-15 percent of total currency deals, so this month it was practically up to the central bank alone to cover demand," Mykola Melnychuk, chief of foreign currency reserves, told Reuters.
The official rate of the hryvnia currency is determined at the daily trading session on the UICE.
The hryvnia fell to 1.800 to the dollar on Tuesday on the exchange from 1.793.
The hryvnia has been falling for most of this month after the central bank stopped intervening on the UICE to maintain the 1.760 rate at which the hryvnia was introduced on September 2.
The central bank has previously suggest tying the hryvnia to a single foreign currency or currency basket.

Melnychuk said the International Monetary Fund, starting a two-week mission visit to Kiev on Tuesday, wants Ukraine to establish a currency corridor as a condition of receiving a $2.5 to $3 billion Extended Fund Facility.
Ukraine has requested that the facility included a $1.5 billion stabilisation fund for the hryvnia.
A currency corridor, already introduced in Russia, is similar to a peg. The central bank sets upper and lower limits for the currency, which is allowed to fluctuate within that range.
